question: Your chat app on Microsoft Foundry must answer prompts that contain **photos** as well as text. What kind of generative AI model do you have to deploy?
answer: A **multimodal model** — one that accepts **image** input (and in some cases **audio**) in addition to text.
explanation: A text-only model cannot handle a prompt that includes an image, so vision-based chat starts with choosing and deploying a multimodal model. Such vision-enabled models do more than name the objects in a picture: some reason over what they see, for example interpreting a chart or judging whether an object is damaged. Everything else in the app — endpoint, prompts, responses — works as in a text-based chat.

question: You build a recipe assistant that answers questions about photos of ingredients. Which **three** models from the Microsoft Foundry model catalog are multimodal and can take the photo as input?
explanation: These are the multimodal examples Microsoft Foundry offers among others: a Microsoft model and two OpenAI models. In the course's code, gpt-4.1 is called through the Responses API, while Phi-4-multimodal-instruct goes through the ChatCompletions API, the fallback for models that don't support Responses. The playground screenshot in the course shows gpt-4.1-mini answering a question about a mango photo.

options.why: Microsoft's multimodal Phi model; it accepts text and image input.
An OpenAI model in Foundry that accepts images in a prompt.
The smaller gpt-4.1 variant is also multimodal and accepts image input.
A small text-only Phi model; image input needs the multimodal variant.
An embedding model returns vectors for search, not chat responses to an image.

question: You have deployed a multimodal model in Microsoft Foundry and want to try an image-based prompt **without writing any code**. Where and how do you do it?
answer: In the **chat playground** of the Microsoft Foundry portal: **upload an image from a local file** and add text to the same message.
explanation: The image and the text go into one message, and the model responds to both together — for example a mango photo with "What desserts could I make with this?". The playground is the quick check after deployment. A client app later sends the same kind of mixed message from code, as a multi-part user message with a text item and an image item.
